item.title: UK net migration falls to 77,000, lowest annual level in nearly 30 years
item.description: Net migration to the UK fell to 77,000 for the year to June, the lowest annual figure since 1997 excluding the Covid years, statistics showed on Thursday. The net migration figures – the difference between the numbers of people arriving in and leaving Britain – are a boost for the UK’s centre-left Labour government, which has been under pressure from the hard right anti-immigration Reform UK party on the issue. item.title: Singapore doctor remanded over filming 874 women in Melbourne: ‘abhorrent sexual predator’
item.description: A Singaporean trainee surgeon who secretly filmed hundreds of his female colleagues in Australian hospitals was remanded on Thursday. Ryan Cho, 29, will be sentenced on February 12 after he pleaded guilty to recording 874 women at three major Melbourne hospitals and shared houses, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation. item.title: China’s tech ambitions to stay on track despite Shanghai party chief’s ouster: analysts
item.description: The ousting of Shanghai Communist Party chief Chen Jining, a prominent technocrat who championed the city’s artificial intelligence and semiconductor sectors, could heighten scrutiny of state-backed tech investments, although analysts see little sign of a shift in China’s broader tech ambitions. item.title: Hong Kong lawmakers defend CUHK ordinance changes as move to boost governance
item.description: Lawmakers have defended proposed amendments to the ordinance of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), saying the changes will strengthen how the institution is governed. Legislators Jonathan Leung Chun and Bill Tang Ka-piu, who sit on the institution’s governing council, said on Thursday that much of the ordinance’s content had failed to keep pace with current societal and legislative changes, necessitating the amendments. item.title: UN experts demand Vietnam explain ‘abduction’ of activists from Cambodia
item.description: Vietnam must explain how three pro-democracy activists ended up in detention facing terrorism charges after being allegedly abducted from neighbouring Cambodia, United Nations experts said on Thursday. Vietnam permits little to no dissent within its borders and critics say its security apparatus stretches abroad, with wanted dissidents previously abducted in Thailand and Germany.
